model.parameter_domain_description: See the parameter registry and the domain of each theorem; the dimension may be any finite integer.
description_paragraphs: The function $a$ is $\mu_x$-strongly convex and $\beta_x$-smooth; $b$ is $\mu_y$-strongly convex and $\beta_y$-smooth. These conditions hold on the respective full Euclidean spaces.
Assume $B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y\times d_x}$ and $\|B\|_{\rm op}\le\beta_{xy}$. A positive smallest singular value is not promised. The unique saddle point $(x^\star,y^\star)$ exists.

public_inputs: Dimensions, exact domain descriptions, accuracy, declared upper and lower parameter bounds, and an initial point when used.
description_paragraphs: Dimensions, domains, initial point, tolerance, and parameters marked public are supplied before querying. Analytic representations of the hidden functions or operators are not disclosed.

$$
x\mapsto\nabla a(x),\quad y\mapsto\nabla b(y),\quad v\mapsto Bv,\quad u\mapsto B^\top u.
$$
Every interface is exact. The quantities $a,b,B$ are hidden; left and right matrix products may be chosen separately. No proximal mapping or linear-system solve is supplied.

objects.definition: $\Phi(x)=a(x)+\sup_{y\in\mathbb R^{d_y}}\{y^{\mathsf T}Bx-b(y)\}$. Strong convexity of $b$ ensures a finite inner minimum and a unique minimizer.
The function $a:\mathbb R^{d_x}\to\mathbb R$ is $\mu_x$-strongly convex and $\beta_x$-smooth in Euclidean norm.
The function $b:\mathbb R^{d_y}\to\mathbb R$ is $\mu_y$-strongly convex and $\beta_y$-smooth in the Euclidean norm.
Require $B\in\mathbb R^{d_y\times d_x}$ and $\|B\|_{\rm op}\le\beta_{xy}$. The matrix is accessible only through products with it and its transpose.

norms.definition: Euclidean norm; multilinear operator norm induced by Euclidean norms

bracket.envelope_certificate: Both formulas refer to the same weights and a single achievable vector. Expanded log in upper depends on conditioning, so joint-parameter constant-factor closure is not asserted.

notes: This profile sets both minimum-singular-value promises for the source coupling matrix to zero, retaining only its spectral-norm bound. The richer spectral family is recorded as additional coverage. Both initialization logarithms and all three operation costs remain explicit.
